title: Multi-agent orchestration
task_statement: Design multi-agent work with clear handoffs, isolated context, and a merge step owned by one agent. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Subagent delegation
components.first_principle: Each subagent keeps its own conversation history, and the lead agent receives only the subagent's reported results.
steps: List each subagent that the lead agent can call in the multiagent block.
Give each subagent a system prompt and tools for one scope.
The lead agent delegates a bounded task to each subagent.
Each subagent works in its own session thread.
The lead agent reads each subagent report and merges the results.
Send a follow-up message to a subagent when its report needs more work.
pros: Subagents work with isolated context, so their histories do not mix.
Specialist prompts and tool sets keep each subagent focused.
A subagent thread stays available for follow-up messages.
cons: A session can have at most 25 child threads at a time, idle ones included.
Every agent in a run uses tokens, so cost rises with each subagent.
use_when: The work splits into well-scoped tasks that feed one goal.
Specialists need different system prompts or tools.
The lead agent must check in with a subagent after its report.
do_not_use_when: Each subtask needs the result of the previous subtask. (Inference)
One agent with all tools completes the task inside the latency limit. (Inference)

constraints.combination: Compare the total latency with one agent run before you add subagents. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Set a session budget that caps the spend of all child threads.
List the allowed subagents in the predefined_agents list of subagents.
constraints.combination: Set inline_agents to disabled, because inline agents are on by default.

constraints.choice: Read each thread through the session event stream.

components.exam_tie: D1.4. Expect independent specialist work with a deadline. The credited answer uses a lead agent, scoped subagents, and a merge step. (Inference)
components.trap: Three agents with no lead and no merge. Each agent returns output, and no one owns one coherent result. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Delegate only independent, well-scoped work, and keep one lead agent that owns the merge.
components.exam_tip: If the stem needs one coherent result, pick the option with a named lead and a merge step. (Inference)

components.name: Dynamic workflow runs
components.first_principle: Claude writes a program that calls many agents in phases and combines their results without the lead agent in each step.
steps: Tell the agent in its system prompt when to use a workflow run.
The agent writes a workflow with phases and the agents for each phase.
The server runs the workflow in the background as one workflow run.
Context and results pass from one agent to the next in code.
Check the run by its phases, and read each thread while the run is active.
pros: The main session stays free to talk with the user.
Runs suit work that has many pieces that can run in parallel.
Phases give named progress points for each run.
cons: You cannot send follow-up messages to a run's threads.
The server archives each run thread by the end of its run.
Each agent in a run uses tokens, so each run needs a budget.
use_when: The work has many pieces that run in parallel.
A long task should finish sooner through parallel phases.
Audits, migrations, deep research, and cross-checks fit a run.
do_not_use_when: The lead agent must send follow-up instructions to each worker during the work.
The task has one judgment step and no parallel pieces. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Set a session budget before each run.
constraints.combination: Set the budget for the whole session, because runs count toward it. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Read thread output while the run is active.
constraints.combination: The server archives each thread at the end of its run.

constraints.choice: List the allowed agents in the predefined_agents list of workflows, and disable inline_agents.
constraints.combination: Pin each listed agent to a version number.

constraints.choice: Use a run for long work that should complete sooner.
constraints.combination: Split the run into phases with parallel agents in each phase.

components.exam_tie: D1.4. Expect a large parallel job with a progress need. The credited answer uses a workflow run with phases and a session budget. (Inference)
components.trap: A chat with each agent in turn. The sequence removes the parallel work that the run could split. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Use a workflow run for many-piece parallel work, and cap its spend with a session budget.
components.exam_tip: If the stem asks for a follow-up to each worker, pick subagents, not a workflow run. (Inference)

patterns.wording: independent specialist work with one deadline
patterns.answer_type: lead agent with scoped subagents and a merge
patterns.rule: Split on independent seams. Keep one lead that owns the merge.
traps: One agent in sequence for independent tracks

patterns.wording: many parallel pieces and a progress need
patterns.answer_type: workflow run with phases and a budget
patterns.rule: Use a workflow run. Cap spend with a session budget.
traps: Chat with each agent in turn

patterns.wording: entangled steps that share one context that changes over time
patterns.rule: Keep one agent when each step needs the previous result.
traps: Parallel workers that each need the full history
